newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW - no solution in sight in dispute with EU.
newsitem.headline: VW - no solution in sight in dispute with EU.

text.p: Volkswagen AG is again at odds with the European Union over plant subsidies, rejecting on Monday European Commission demands that it repay grants received from the state of Saxony.

A VW spokesman said the company should not be forced to repay a disputed 91 million marks it received from the eastern German state and that a "mutually agreeable and lasting solution" to ongoing disputes over subsidies should be reached.
At issue is some 540 million marks of Saxony state subsidies which the EC cleared VW to receive in June 1996.

The figure was 241 million marks less than VW and Saxony had originally agreed upon and the subsidy had been hotly contested by the EC as anti-competitive and an unfair advantage for the German carmaker.

But rather than paying out only the 540 million marks, Saxony granted VW a 631 million mark investment, leaving VW with 91 million marks more than the EC had agreed. The funds are now are in a bank account, the VW spokesman said.
VW has suggested that it step up investment in order to offset the additional state subsidies but EC competition officials remain angered by the overpayment.
German business daily Handelsblatt quoted European Commission competition official Alexander Schaub as saying that the EC would demand repayment of all grants blocked by it in the June 1996 ruling.
Until VW paid back those funds, the EC would block any further subsidies for VW projects, the newspaper said in its Monday edition.
